title: Copenhagen construction-worker gathering at the opening of OK23 construction bargaining
participants_original: Netavisen Pio reports that, according to organizers, around 1,000 construction workers gathered at Rådhuspladsen to support 3F negotiators going to Dansk Industri.
threshold_50_evidence: S019 reports an organizer-attributed approximate attendance of around 1,000 workers physically present at the Copenhagen square; this reported estimate exceeds 50, but is not an exact count or independently corroborated by an opened body.

start_date.summary: The report dates the gathering to Thursday, 12 January 2023.

end_date.summary: The report describes support for negotiators going to Dansk Industri but gives no physical end time or end date beyond the event date; leave the end unknown.

location.summary: The gathering was at Rådhuspladsen in Copenhagen.

organizer.summary: The report attributes the estimate to organizers and identifies 3F negotiators and a union speaker, but does not identify the formal event organizer.

demands.summary: Higher wages and measures against social dumping are stated as construction workers’ key bargaining demands; the article frames the immediate gathering as support for negotiators headed to private employer Dansk Industri.

participants_original.summary: Pio reports “around 1,000” and attributes the estimate to organizers.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The one opened account’s organizer-attributed approximate count is well above 50; retain its attribution and do not treat it as an exact count.

protester_violence.summary: The read article does not report demonstrator violence; silence is not coded as explicit absence.

state_response.summary: The read article does not describe event-specific state response; all response dimensions remain unknown.

notes: This is a physical gathering with a reported estimate above the threshold, but the documented immediate target is employer-side collective bargaining. Pio says a proposal to abolish a holiday (probably Store Bededag) and working hours were also important topics, but it does not establish a demand addressed to the Danish government at this gathering. Do not code those topics as a state demand without further evidence. S001 body access failed technically; S002 is a participant-post discovery lead; S020-S022 remain search-only and are not treated as independent body corroboration.
open_questions: Did participants make a demand to the Danish government or its policy, rather than support employer-side bargaining only?
Was the proposed Store Bededag abolition a demand at this gathering or only a wider issue described as important?
Is there an independent contemporary body source for attendance and demands?
When did the physical gathering end, and did any state response occur?

title: Possible Copenhagen anti-fur gathering outside Louis Vuitton
participants_original: The Q019 search-result snippet says a group of people demonstrated at Amagertorv 2 on Saturday afternoon; it gives no number.
threshold_50_evidence: No count or clear 50-plus description is available. “A group” does not establish the threshold. The article body was not obtained.

start_date.summary: The search-result snippet dates the described Saturday-afternoon gathering to 21 January 2023; body unverified.

location.summary: The search-result snippet names Amagertorv 2; its headline identifies Louis Vuitton.

participants_original.summary: The snippet says “a group of people” and supplies no numerical estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No number or qualitative lower bound of 50 appears in the captured snippet.

possible_relation.summary: S011 says the previous weekend a group protested outside Louis Vuitton with the same message as its Jan 28 Max Mara event. The date/location fit the S018 lead, but shared identity or an organized continuous campaign is unconfirmed.

notes: Search-only lead, not body-verified. S018’s first exact-URL open returned Cache miss; no retry was made. S011’s opened Jan 28 article refers to a similar Louis Vuitton action the previous weekend, but neither organizer identity nor continuity is established. Keep this possible action separate from Jan 28.
open_questions: Can the S018 article body be read through an allowed route or corroborated by an independent contemporary source?
What were the actual organizer, demands, physical attendee count, start/end, and target?
Was this the Louis Vuitton action mentioned by S011, and was either action aimed at Danish government policy?

title: CAFT fur protest outside Max Mara in Copenhagen
organizer: Coalition to Abolish the Fur Trade (CAFT) activists (reported by S016)
participants_original: S011 describes a group; S016 identifies CAFT activists but gives no number or 50-plus estimate.
threshold_50_evidence: The two opened accounts give no numerical estimate or qualitative indication that 50 or more people attended; threshold remains unresolved.

start_date.summary: S011 dates the gathering to Saturday 28 January; S016, published Monday 30 January, says the action took place Saturday afternoon, also 28 January.

end_date.summary: S016 says police stopped the action within a few minutes; this supports an end on 28 January but not an exact clock time or duration.

location.summary: Both place the fur protest outside Max Mara in central Copenhagen; S011 identifies Strøget.

organizer.summary: S016 identifies activists from Coalition to Abolish the Fur Trade (CAFT).

demands.summary: The described demand concerned fur use and Max Mara’s sale of mink/fox fur, a private retailer target. No Danish-government demand is reported; the allowed local demand taxonomy has no matching fur category.

participants_original.summary: S011 says “a group”; S016 gives no attendee count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Neither article supports a 50-person lower bound.

state_response.summary: S016 reports that police stopped the action within minutes, handcuffed and administratively detained one activist, and shoved two others. S011 describes police presence as calm and for public order. Preserve both accounts; no primary police record was reviewed.

protester_violence.summary: Neither reviewed account reports demonstrator violence; silence is not coded as explicit absence.

notes: The event physically occurred and its action date/end day are reported, but the 50-person threshold is not established and the reported target is a private retailer, with no demand to the Danish government stated. S011 says the gathering stayed calm with police present; S016 says police forcefully ended it within minutes. The descriptions differ; do not resolve the response conflict from these two reports. Linked photographs/video were not inspected. The shared episode key with E002 is a tentative review link, not a merge.
open_questions: Did at least 50 people physically participate?
Was any demand directed to Danish government or its policy, or was this exclusively a private retailer dispute?
What explains the differing reports of police conduct, and what was the exact physical end time?
Was this action organized by the same group as the possible Jan 21 Louis Vuitton event?
